You are researching the spherical two-electron Lieb-Oxford ratio.
You may propose only bounded density data, not executable code. The fixed evaluator
uses rho=A*r^alpha*exp(-r+sum Gaussian bumps)*T((R-r)/width)^2, T(u)=3u^2-2u^3
clipped to [0,1]. A normalizes the 3D density to two electrons. Every candidate is
verified by grid refinement and two coordinate integrations. Do not edit checks.
Return ONE JSON object with keys action,hypothesis,candidates. action is evaluate
or finish. hypothesis is a short public research rationale, NOT private reasoning.
For evaluate, candidates is a list of 1-4 objects with alpha,radius,width,bumps.
alpha in [0,2], radius in [3,30], width in [0.1,radius/2]. bumps is a list of 0-4
objects with amplitude in [-3,3], center in [0,radius], sigma in [0.1,radius].
For finish, candidates must be []. Ground claims in tool results, distinguish
failed checks, numerical evidence and mathematical proof. Compare with the
historical lambda=1.701052, not a current-record assertion. No global optimality.
Use feedback to revise density shapes. Give no unverified claims of discovery.

{"definition": "lambda=(D-V_SCE)/(C_x*integral rho^(4/3)); C_x=(3/4)(3/pi)^(1/3)", "historical_benchmark": {"lambda": 1.701052, "preprint": "https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.01715", "source": "Seidl, Vuckovic, Gori-Giorgi (2016), Eq. (60)", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1080/00268976.2015.1136440", "warning": "A historical comparator, not a verified current record. Beating it does not establish novelty."}, "limits": "No assertion of a physical Coulomb ground-state density. Finite kinetic admissibility of a density does not make the singular SCE coupling a finite-kinetic wavefunction.", "previous_fixed_experiments": {"exponential_lambda": 1.69905243, "hard_cutoff_parameters": {"alpha": 0.5, "radius": 13.69}, "hard_cutoff_r_half_exp_lambda": 1.700974139, "untruncated_r_half_exp_lambda": 1.700965186, "warning": "Hard cutoff generally gives sqrt(rho) outside H1; it is only an SCE/classical benchmark."}, "research_objective": "Propose smooth compactly supported densities and local perturbations, test and revise using independent numerical checks.", "scope": "N=2, spherical three-dimensional densities; this subset cannot settle the universal Lieb-Oxford constant", "verification": "Normalization, refinement and different integration variables. Shared CDF inverse means cross-checks are not fully algorithmically independent. No interval certification."}
